summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with a history of chronic pancreatitis, was admitted with a five-day history of epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and oliguria. She was managed with NPO status, IV hydration, and pain control using non-narcotic medications due to allergies. Her symptoms improved over the course of the admission, with resolution of leukocytosis and return of normal urine output. She gradually advanced to a regular diet and tolerated oral medications. No imaging or procedures were performed. She was discharged home in stable condition with no changes to her medication regimen and instructions to follow up with her primary care provider.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
